evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError is the abstract base; ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError all extend it and are used by order.ts and product.ts
src/domain/order.ts: Order constructor calls assertPositiveInteger imported from ./product rather than repeating the quantity rule
src/domain/order.ts: the transition rules are only in FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATES, nextState(), canCancel(), advanceTo() and cancel()
src/domain/product.ts: the stock rules are in Product.available, canReserve, reserve, release and consumeReserved
src/domain/repositories.ts: ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator and Clock are only port interfaces typed on the domain's Order, OrderState and Product
Minor: assertPositiveInteger is in product.ts, and Clock and IdGenerator are in repositories.ts; both are naming or placement issues, not breaks in cohesion
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The four files form one domain model for orders and stock. errors.ts defines a single DomainError hierarchy that order.ts and product.ts use throughout. The rules for each entity are kept inside it. Order owns the state machine (FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE_STATES, advanceTo, cancel). Product owns the stock invariants (available = stockOnHand − reserved, reserve, release, consumeReserved). repositories.ts declares only the ports (interfaces) the application and infrastructure layers depend on. order.ts reuses product.ts's assertPositiveInteger instead of writing its own check, so that rule lives in one place. Minor issues, none of which breaks the rule: (1) assertPositiveInteger is a general validation helper but sits in product.ts. (2) Clock and IdGenerator are in a file named repositories.ts, though they are still domain ports. (3) FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE repeats most of ORDER_STATES in the same file. (4) release and consumeReserved repeat the same "quantity > reserved" check inside one class. None of these splits the module into unrelated concerns, spreads an invariant across files, or bypasses the module's abstractions.
